prompt: Real gerrymanders get nicknames based on their shape (the original was 'the Gerry-mander,' a salamander). Design a district and give it its inevitable animal nickname.
response: Whole tradition kicked off back in 1812, when Governor Elbridge Gerry up in Massachusetts signed off on a district so twisted folks said it looked like a salamander — the Gerry-mander. So here's mine, buddy. Big round body sitting on the good side of the county, a long skinny neck reaching way up north to grab the two towns I want, and a little curl of a tail down south for the lake. Call her the Seahorse. Fits her to a T.
